newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks start with modest gains, BNP rises.
newsitem.headline: French stocks start with modest gains, BNP rises.

text.p: French shares retreated slightly after posting small advances at the opening on Tuesday after a three-day break for Armistice Day.
The underlying trend was positive, though, buoyed by Wall Street's continued run-up, traders said.
Bank BNP shot up three percent, after the UAP-Axa merger news, on a view an expected share swap would reduce the bank's capital loss on its UAP stake.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 1.09 points or 0.05 percent at 2,204.11 at 0912 GMT, after opening up 0.06 percent. The CAC-40 futures contract was unchanged at 2,210 from Friday's close.
Volume was a heavy 900 million francs.
"It's going to be a very good day," said one broker, referring to the UAP-Axa news. "It's good news for the sector."

Insurer AGF surged 3.61 percent to 163.50 francs on speculation it would hit a targeted 10 percent return on equity sooner than expected as it will be forced to restructure more aggressively to compete with the new UAP-Axa.

There was "huge action" on BNP, which climbed 3.35 percent to 206.6 francs as the rumoured UAP-Axa stock swap at between 130-160 francs per UAP share would be at a premium to UAP's Friday close at 116.90 francs. BNP is UAP's main shareholder with some 17.5 percent.
A block of 850,000 Valeo shares changed hands at 314 francs per share
LVMH gains 0.72 percent to 1,256 francs, helped by nine-month sales, seen as positive.
Pechiney slips 2.81 percent to 224.5 francs. Its U.S. American National Can subsidiary lost a legal dispute over patents and will take a $102 million hit in 1996 results.

Eurotunnel falls 1.32 percent to 7.50 francs, as an alleged insider trading scandal on the troubled 1994 rights issue rumbles on, with the British authorities set to probe the London side of the rights issue.
